items.title: THE SIX IN THE BAR
items.why: Your six supplies sit in the top bar while you travel, and A is in the game now with B and C as other layouts. You see it on the MAP in the RUN tab.

items.title: THE GROUND UNDER THE FIGHTERS, CLEANED UP
items.why: The ovals, blocks and words are gone from the fight's ground, and it draws at your phone's real pixels. You see it in the VOTE tab under LOOK, and in the fight in the RUN tab.

items.title: YOUR PEOPLE HAVE KIDS. THEY ARE THE NEXT ACT'S COMPANY.
items.why: Your people have kids, and the kids are the next act's company, unless one falls early with no kid. You see it in the VOTE tab under LOOK, shot on the real phone across three acts.

items.title: GROK SAYS YOU GAVE IT SIX PILES: MEDICINE, BATTERIES, RESOURCES, CLOUT, AMMO, TOOLS
items.why: Grok says you split the money into six different piles, and thumbs up switches to Grok's six. You see it only as text in the VOTE tab; in the game the piles sit in the top bar on the MAP.

show.src:
GROK'S SIX (from your chat with it, unverified): medicine, batteries, resources (food + gas + water), clout (a score, not spent), ammunition, tools. A car shot spends the resources pile.

THE OLD SIX (rule 47): batteries, food, meds, rounds, tape, water.

YES = Grok's six. NO = the old six.

items.title: VIA GROK: THE CAR IS THE HANDGONNE
items.why: The car is our handgonne: a short loud cone shot that spends gas and eats the turn to reload. You see it only as text in the VOTE tab; up builds it into the fight.

show.src:
BATTLE BROTHERS' HANDGONNE: 35 to 75 damage, a cone, range 2, fire 3 AP, reload 9 AP, cannot fire and reload in one turn.

OURS, VIA GROK: the car. Ram or a blast from the lane. The shot is gas, so it spends the resources pile.

Seen in: the fight (COMBAT), round two.

items.title: VIA GROK: THE DEAD ARE BODIES WITH A CHIP STILL IN THEM
items.why: The walking dead are bodies with a lab chip still in them, and the necromancer holds the controller. You see it only as text in the VOTE tab; it is NOT IN A TAB YET in the game.

show.src:
VIA GROK, FROM YOUR CHAT: humans stay people (eight factions). The dead are chipped bodies, analog horror, not magic. The necromancer is the person with the controller.

STILL PROPOSALS: orcs = driverless heavy machines, goblins = drones.

Seen in: the fight (COMBAT), the roster file.

items.title: VIA GROK: THE FIRST FIGHT'S SIX WEAPONS
items.why: The first fight's six weapons: pistol, car, rifle, sledge, car door as a shield, and things to throw. You see it only as text in the VOTE tab; up builds them into the fight.

show.src:
THE SIX: pistol (dagger, 1 tile). Car (handgonne, cone, reload). Rifle (crossbow, one hard shot then rack). Sledge (hammer, breaks armour and doors). Car door (shield). Bottles, bricks, flares (throw).

NOT YET: no bow, no flame line, no mortar until the second district.

Seen in: the fight (COMBAT).

items.title: VIA GROK: MELEE IS THE NEXT TILE AND SPENDS NOTHING; GUNS SPEND AMMO
items.why: Melee reaches the next tile and spends nothing, while guns spend ammo. You see it only as text in the VOTE tab; up builds it into the fight.

show.src:
RANGE AT HOUSE SCALE: 1 tile = melee, the next house or the gap. 2 = across the street: shotgun, spike strip, a thrown bottle. 3 to 6 = the rifle. 7 to 13 = a roof gun, only if you say so.

THE REWARD: a melee hit costs no ammo. A gun hit costs one round.

Seen in: the fight (COMBAT), round two.

items.title: THE FLOOR, ROUND TWO: NO GRID
items.why: A street is one tile with houses on both edges, and the grid and circles are gone from the ground. You see it in the VOTE tab under LOOK, and in the fight in the RUN tab.

items.title: THE STREET HAS KERBS
items.why: The fight's street has gutters, two lanes, a faint yellow line, kerbs and sidewalks. You see it in the VOTE tab under LOOK, and in the fight in the RUN tab.

items.title: VIA GROK: THE FIRST FIGHT, ONE SHEET A BUILDER CAN CODE
items.why: Grok's first fight on one sheet: an 8 by 6 board, you alone with a pistol, a pipe and the car against six road crew. You see it only as text in the VOTE tab; up builds it as the demo's first fight.

show.src:
THE SLICE: 8 by 6 house tiles. Street down the middle. You south, six road crew north, five tiles apart. You: pistol (1 tile, spends ammo, ignores armour), pipe (1 tile, stun, spends nothing), the car on the south edge (cone at 2 tiles, spends gas, reload eats the turn). Them: four pipes, one car door, one pistol. Win: all six down or fleeing; pay in batteries and a post to hire one person.

FIXED TO YOUR LOCKS: you are downed, never dead. Everything costs one.

Seen in: the fight (COMBAT), the demo's first fight.

items.title: A TRADER FACING YOU
items.why: Facing you, haggling and bowing barely moved, and now he offers a palm and shrugs, and the bow dips with an arm sweeping out. You see it in the VOTE tab under LOOK, before beside after on the beat.
items.said: once you understand the scale of how far you can zoom out and zoom in, that's really important to me

items.title: THE FIGHT'S FLOOR: YOUR STREET UNDER THE FIGHTERS
items.why: The ground under the fight is now your own street art, house-sized: road with its kerbs and faded line, a crossing, a big street, a freeway lane, two gravel lots, a driveway slab and a flat roof you can stand on, plus a dead car and a block wall for cover. Thumbs up and combat drops them under the fighters, and you see it in the COMBAT tab when a fight starts.

items.title: THE SETTLEMENT SCREEN: SEE THE PLACE, TAP A BUILDING
items.why: You arrive and tap a building: a camp has the hall, the job board, the stall and scavenge, a town adds the barber and the bar, a fortress adds the clinic and the training yard, and each one talks through a face. You see it in the VOTE tab under LOOK, a working screen you can drag, NOT IN A TAB YET until the run plugs it into arriving on the map.

items.title: THE FIGHT'S COVER: A CAR, A WALL, A SHED
items.why: The tan cardboard blocks are replaced by seven things a man can hide behind: your three dead cars, a block wall in three shapes (straight, a corner, knocked through) and a rusted backyard shed, all on the new calmer floor. Thumbs up and combat puts them on the board, and you see it in the COMBAT tab when a fight starts.

items.said: the sidewalks are way too fucking big... everything we do is 45 when it comes to the land underneath
items.title: THE FIGHT'S FLOOR, REAL SIDEWALKS, SEEN AT 45
items.why: The sidewalks are now real Vegas size, about an eighth of the road, and the ground is seen from the 45 camera so kerbs, roof walls and car sides show. Thumbs up and combat drops it under the fighters, and you see it in the COMBAT tab when a fight starts.

items.title: THE WHOLE BATTLE BROTHERS LOOP, UGLY, IN ONE FILE
items.why: Travel the map at up to 5x, arrive at a place, take a job at the board, walk onto it, fight a crew on house tiles until it ends, get paid, hire at the hall, and pay wages at night, all of it working end to end with placeholder art. You see it in the VOTE tab under LOOK, NOT IN A TAB YET until the run folds it into the demo and the art lanes dress it.

items.title: TWO FIGHT BOARDS: THE CUL-DE-SAC AND THE DESERT WASH
items.why: Two whole fight boards that are places, not a straight street: a cul-de-sac with six houses round the turnaround and their driveways, and a dry desert wash snaking through creosote with rocks to hide behind and one outcrop for high ground. Thumbs up and combat cuts fights from these, and you see it in the COMBAT tab when a fight starts on a suburb or desert cell.

items.title: COVER IS A THING
items.why: The tan boxes in the fight are now the second combat chat's dead cars, block walls and shed, and the rings and red bars at the enemies' feet moved over their heads. You see it in the COMBAT tab, where a parked car is now one tile instead of six.

items.title: FOUR MORE FIGHT BOARDS: SUBURB, STRIP LOT, SCRUB, FREEWAY
items.why: Four more places a fight can start: a suburb street with houses both sides, a dead strip mall parking lot, open desert scrub, and eight lanes of jammed freeway, and every tile now says if it is rough ground, high ground or a wall, like Battle Brothers. Thumbs up and combat cuts fights from these, and you see it in the COMBAT tab when a fight starts on that kind of map cell.

items.title: EVERY FIGHT ENDS
items.why: When the last man drops or the rest run off, the fight now ends and pays out, instead of waiting quietly for you to walk to the way out, which is why your fight never ended. You see it in the COMBAT tab: win a fight and the receipt comes up the moment nobody is left to shoot.

items.title: THE FIGHT'S FLOOR: THE TILES BELOW THE PEOPLE
items.why: Two chats cut this floor the same round and the combat one is shaped right for the board, so judge this one only on the ground material: your own street bank, one pixel to one pixel, instead of a stretched smear. You see it in the VOTE tab, three panels: your old board, the same frame with the new floor, and the pixels up close.

items.title: THREE MORE FIGHT BOARDS: THE SHORE, THE LANDFILL, THE RUIN
items.why: Three more places a fight can start: the dried-up lake shore where you wade at the edge of black water, the city dump with trash heaps as high ground, and a burnt-out block where half the roofs fell in. Thumbs up and combat cuts fights from these, and you see it in the COMBAT tab when a fight starts on that kind of map cell.

items.title: THE MAP NOW USES EVERY PIXEL OF YOUR PHONE
items.why: The map painted one dot for every nine pixels on your phone and now it paints every one, left is before and right is now, and travelling got smoother, not slower. You see it on the map, the first screen of the demo after loading.

items.title: THE GROUND IS 45 DEGREES
items.why: The fight's ground is now seen at 45 degrees like you ruled, and the street is one tile with real thin sidewalks and kerbs instead of a sidewalk as wide as a house. You see it in the COMBAT tab, standing on the second combat chat's street and dirt lots.

items.title: THE MAP ICONS ARE THE GAME'S OWN PEOPLE AND BUILDINGS
items.why: You said the icons suck, so the blobs are gone: crowds are three real dressed people, crews are two people walking under their faction's flag, and home bases are a fort, a town or a trailer camp with a flag on it. You see it on the map, the first screen of the demo after loading.

items.title: FIGHTS AT NIGHT: THE ONLY LIGHT IS WHAT STILL WORKS
items.why: The suburb street and the strip lot after dark: black except where one street lamp in three still burns and where people keep fire barrels going, and only those lit squares let you shoot and see like daytime. Thumbs up and combat uses these for night fights, and you see it in the COMBAT tab when a fight starts after sundown.

items.title: VIA GROK: TEN WIKI CROWNS ARE ONE BATTERY, AND ONE BATTERY IS THE FLOOR
items.why: Grok says you told it there are no crowns: every Battle Brothers price is divided by ten into batteries, and nothing costs less than one; thumbs up and every wiki price converts that way. You see it only as text in the VOTE tab, and in the game in every price at the settlement screen's stall and hall.

show.src:
VIA GROK, FROM YOUR CHAT: 10 crowns = 1 battery. The floor is 1 battery. The shop's town markup applies first, then divide by ten. A level's 2-crown raise adds up to 1 battery every five levels. A bought (indebted) man costs batteries up front and 0 a day.

Seen in: the settlement screen's stall and posts (RUN TWO), the top bar.

items.title: VIA GROK: YOU SEE THE WHOLE PERSON BEFORE YOU PAY, AND THE GEAR COMES WITH THEM
items.why: Grok says you told it the hidden hire was the worst part of Battle Brothers, so a hire shows face, past, stats and traits before you pay, with their gear included; thumbs up builds the hall that way. You see it only as text in the VOTE tab, and in the game at the hall in the settlement screen.

show.src:
VIA GROK, FROM YOUR CHAT: no tryout, no fee to look. The row shows face, past, stats, stars, traits. The button spends 20 to 1,000 batteries and buys the person and their kit. Daily pay from the wage table after; a bought man pays 0 a day.

Seen in: the settlement screen's posts (RUN TWO).

items.title: HOUSES THAT LOOK LIKE HOUSES, ON A BATTLE BROTHERS SIZED BOARD
items.why: The houses now have a real tile roof, a front wall with a door and garage, and a shadow, and the fight board is 20 houses across and 15 deep with the two sides starting five houses apart. Thumbs up and combat fights on boards this big, and you see it in the COMBAT tab when a fight starts.

items.title: REACH IS LIT
items.why: In a fight, the houses your gun can reach now glow faintly, the eight around you with a pistol, two out with a rifle and three with a scope, and a man you can shoot glows brighter. You see it in the COMBAT tab whenever you are in cover.

items.title: THE LOOP IS THE DEMO: TOWN, JOB, FIGHT, PAY
items.why: Walk to a town and its screen opens, take a job off the board, the job shows up on the map with a red flag, go there and fight, clear it and you get paid, walk away and the job waits for you. You see it in the demo: tap the town next to you, CHURCH, two blocks away.

items.title: REAL STORE FRONTS, AND THE NEW HOUSES ON EVERY BLOCK
items.why: The strip mall now has real store fronts (blank sign, dark glass, a boarded window, the door), and the cul-de-sac and the burnt block use the new 3-D houses, the burnt ones caved in to the beams. Thumbs up and combat uses these blocks, and you see it in the COMBAT tab when a fight starts.

items.title: THE FRONT DOOR: DIFFICULTY, ORIGIN AND A NAME
items.why: While the valley loads you pick how hard the fights are, how bare the shelves are, which of fifteen crews you were (Battle Brothers' origins, ours), and your crew's name, and every number on a card is what the game really does. You see it on the loading screen, the first thing the demo shows.

items.title: THE VALLEY HAS AN EDGE: MOUNTAINS, LAKE MEAD AND THE ROADS OUT
items.why: Zoomed all the way out, the city is no longer a square on brown: it sits in a valley between the Spring Mountains, the Sheep Range, Frenchman and the Black Mountains, with Lake Mead and the 15, 95 and 93 running out, all named. You see it on the map when you pinch all the way out.

items.title: THE REBUILT FIGHT IS THE DEMO'S FIGHT
items.why: Every fight on the map now opens the new Battle Brothers fight on the board of the block you stand on, and when it ends you are back on the map in about two seconds, paid if you won the job. You see it in the demo the first time a crew or a job fight starts.

items.title: ZOOMED OUT, THE CITY IS PAINTED
items.why: Pulled all the way out, the city is no longer a grid carpet under giant town icons: every block is painted (roofs, streets, towers that stand up, the rim rising into the ranges) and the towns shrink with the ground the way Battle Brothers does it. You see it on the map when you pinch all the way out.

items.title: INTO A FIGHT THROUGH CLOUDS, AND ZOOMED ALL THE WAY IN
items.why: Going into a fight now rolls through drifting pixel clouds that hold until the fight is built and part on two beats, and coming home goes back through them; and the map now zooms in until a block's own building art sits at your phone's own pixels. You see it the first time a fight starts, and when you pinch all the way in on the map.

items.title: PAST THE MAP THE VALLEY STAYS, AND IT HAS ONE LIGHT
items.why: Pinching out past the map no longer drops to a flat blue sky and a slab: the same land and painted city run to a curved horizon under a dust sky, with no label, and at night the land outside the city goes dark exactly as the city does. You see it on the map when you pinch out past the widest zoom.

items.title: EIGHT BATTLE BROTHERS SIZED BOARDS FOR THE NEW FIGHT
items.why: Eight full fight boards, each 20 houses across and 15 deep with the two sides five houses apart: suburb, cul-de-sac, strip mall, burnt block, desert, freeway, lake shore and dump, ready for the new combat to load. Thumbs up and the new fight starts on these, and you see it in the COMBAT tab once the new fight is in.

items.title: THE FIGHT, STARTED OVER: BATTLE BROTHERS' RULES ON OUR HOUSE TILES
items.why: Twelve of yours against a road crew on COMBAT TWO's suburb and desert boards, with Battle Brothers' 9 action points, hit chances, armour, head hits, injuries, morale and running, every number copied from their wiki, a whole fight in about 2 to 3 minutes. Tap a lit tile twice to walk and a red man twice to swing (AUTO plays your crew), and you see it in the VOTE tab, NOT IN A TAB YET until the run puts it in the loop.

items.title: VIA GROK: WHAT FOOD IS LEFT TEN YEARS IN, ONE WINNER PER STACK
items.why: Grok picked what food survives ten years of Vegas heat, one winner in each of six stacks; thumbs up and the economy chat makes those the food list, thumbs down and food stays one plain pile. You see it only as text in the VOTE tab, and in the game as the food in the top bar and at the stall.

show.src:
VIA GROK, pages GROK_39 to GROK_43: fresh grocery is dead; what lasts is canned, dried, jarred, honey, hard liquor, salt; a hot room halves shelf life. One winner per stack, Grok's picks on the pages.

Seen in: the settlement screen's stall (RUN TWO), the top bar's food count.

items.title: THE NEW FIGHT IS STANDING ON THE NEW GROUND
items.why: Screenshots from the new fight on a phone: the cul-de-sac and the desert, first the whole board as the fight opens, then zoomed in on your crew, and the desert creek no longer looks boxed in. Thumbs up and this ground stays under every fight, and you see it in the COMBAT tab when a fight starts.

items.title: BATTLE BROTHERS' FIFTY PERKS, WITH OUR NAMES, IN THE NEW FIGHT
items.why: All fifty Battle Brothers perks with a draft name of ours (BUILT LIKE A DOOR is Colossus, HARD HEAD is Steel Brow, DOOR MAN is Shield Expert, READS YOU is Fast Adaptation), and 37 of them already change the new fight by their exact wiki numbers, so a level-4 man really is tougher than a level-1. Tap one of yours in the new fight and you see it under his health bar on his card, in the VOTE tab, NOT IN A TAB YET.

items.title: THE PERKS YOU PRESS: SEVEN BUTTONS ON A MAN'S CARD
items.why: The seven Battle Brothers perks you press are buttons on a man's card now, each at its wiki cost: ON ME pulls your breaking men back to steady, CATCH YOUR BREATH halves his tiredness for the whole turn, SWAP OUT trades places with a friend, COME AT ME calls a man onto him, SIDESTEP walks out of reach with no free swing, IMMOVABLE halves the damage, FIRST OUT THE DOOR puts him first next round, and the enemy uses them too. In a fight, when one of yours has one, you see it as a gold button above WAIT, in the VOTE tab, NOT IN A TAB YET.

items.title: NO MORE COPY-PASTED BOARDS: A REAL STREET GRID
items.why: The fight boards no longer repeat one strip of houses across the screen: houses sit on different lots every block, cross streets cut through, some lots are empty slabs, and one house in six is burnt, shown here inside the new fight on a phone. Thumbs up and every fight board is mixed like this, and you see it in the COMBAT tab when a fight starts.

items.title: CROSS STREETS RUN ALL THE WAY THROUGH
items.why: On every town board the cross streets now run top to bottom through every block like a real street grid instead of stopping at a block's edge, and each board now lists its street lamps and fire barrels so night fights can be lit by them. Thumbs up and the fight uses these boards, and you see it in the COMBAT tab when a fight starts.

items.title: THE SAME FIGHT GROUND, FIVE TIMES LIGHTER
items.why: The fight boards now download in about 5 MB instead of 24 with not one visible pixel changed, so fights open faster on a phone; shown here inside the new fight on the cul-de-sac and the lake shore. Thumbs up and nothing else changes, and you see it in the COMBAT tab when a fight starts.

items.title: THE SETTLEMENT SCREEN, REBUILT LIKE BATTLE BROTHERS
items.why: You said look how Battle Brothers settlements work, so the place is now the game's own 45-degree buildings standing in a town, you tap the building itself to open it, and the row of extra buttons is gone. You see it in the VOTE tab under LOOK, and in the demo every time you arrive at a place on the map.

items.title: SEVEN NEW BUILDINGS: APARTMENTS, CHURCH, SCHOOL, GAS STATION, MOTEL, WAREHOUSE, CASINO BACK
items.why: You asked for many more building types, so here are seven new ones at 45 degrees, each with its own shape you can name from far away, plus two new city blocks that use them: main street and the works. Thumbs up and they go on the fight boards, and you see it in the COMBAT tab when a fight starts in town.

items.title: THE NEW BUILDINGS INSIDE THE NEW FIGHT
items.why: The warehouse, motel, school and the rest inside the actual new fight on a phone, on the strip and suburb boards, with the cross streets running straight past them. Thumbs up and the fight keeps these boards, and you see it in the COMBAT tab when a fight starts.

items.title: THE FIFTY PERK NAMES, TO TALK THROUGH
items.why: All fifty Battle Brothers perks with the name we gave each one (READS YOU for Fast Adaptation, BUILT LIKE A DOOR for Colossus, ON ME for Rally the Troops) and the icon now drawn for it, gold for what a man carries and blue for what you press. Rename any you hate in your notes and the fight picks it up, and you see it on every man's card in the fight, in the VOTE tab, NOT IN A TAB YET.

items.title: THE FIGHT'S BAR, BATTLE BROTHERS' LAYOUT IN CARDBOARD, TAPE AND RECEIPTS
items.why: The fight's controls laid out like Battle Brothers' (faces in turn order across the top, his face and bars bottom left, the skills as cracked-glass squares under your thumbs, END TURN and WAIT at the right) but made of our stuff, a taped-on cardboard bar and receipt-paper buttons, every one big enough for a thumb. Play a fight and you see it at the bottom of the screen, in the VOTE tab, NOT IN A TAB YET.

items.title: THE FREEWAY AND THE DUMP, REDONE
items.why: You said the dump and the freeway looked bad, so both are rebuilt around their real shapes: the freeway between sound walls with a raised divider, a jam of cars and an overpass you can climb onto, and the dump as stepped terraces of trash bales and tyres with a road switchbacking up. Thumbs up and these become the fight boards, and you see it in the COMBAT tab when a fight starts on the freeway or the dump.

items.title: THE LINES RUN THROUGH: SHORELINES AND CREEKS MEET BLOCK TO BLOCK
items.why: Every line that crosses from one block to the next now meets itself: the lake shore, the dump road and the desert track line up, and the dry creeks run the whole board top to bottom and down into the lake. Thumbs up and the fight boards keep this, and you see it in the COMBAT tab when a fight starts in the desert or on the shore.

items.title: YOUR CHARACTERS ARE THE FIGHTERS NOW
items.why: Every man in the new fight is your character art from the bank, the rig in his runway clothes with his own face in the turn strip, walking, swinging, flinching when hit and lying where he falls, and one of your own can be walked through but never two. Play a fight and you see it on the whole board, in the VOTE tab, NOT IN A TAB YET.

items.title: AUTO PLAYS YOUR MEN LIKE BATTLE BROTHERS' AI
items.why: AUTO now does what Battle Brothers' own AI does: shooters climb the roofs first (41% of their turns, up from 6%), the line walks up as a line, shooters stay behind the front man, and your men stop piling every swing on one guy. Tap AUTO in a fight and you see it, in the VOTE tab and the demo, NOT IN A TAB YET.

items.title: PINCH IN PAST THE MAP AND YOU ARE ON THE BLOCK
items.why: Pinching in past the map's closest zoom now drops you onto the block you stand on, drawn from the fight's own street pictures, and you can keep pinching until it is the walk's size while you stay the same size on the street. You see it on the map when you pinch in as far as it goes and then once more.

items.title: SETTLEMENTS AS ONE PLACE: CAMP, TOWN, FORTRESS
items.why: The settlement buildings are now part of one picture instead of a row of options: the barber is a house with a striped pole, the clinic a storefront with a cross, the stall sits on the sidewalk, notices are papered on a wall and the job board is a board on a pole, for a camp, a town and a fortress. Thumbs up and the settlement screen uses these pictures, and you see it in the settlement screen when you enter a place (the dotted boxes are what lights up under your finger).

items.title: AT NIGHT THE FIGHT IS LIT BY THE STREET'S OWN LAMPS
items.why: A night fight goes dark and only the live street lamps and burning drums light it, and a man under a lamp is seen from farther and easy to shoot, so you keep your men out of the light. Fight after dark in the demo and you see it, in the VOTE tab, NOT IN A TAB YET.

items.title: VIA GROK: AN INJURY IS ONE PAIN LINE, NOT FIVE
items.why: Grok reports you said a hurt neck, head, arm, leg or chest all show as one pain line, while the game still picks the body part and its penalty the way Battle Brothers does, and one medicine a day closes it. You see it on a hurt man's card in the fight and in the settlement screen's clinic.

show.src:
VIA GROK, pages GROK_49, GROK_67: one label for the injury trait; the penalty follows the body part; a hit of 10 or more health that is a big enough share of max health can leave it; bandages, ibuprofen and super glue all treat it.

Seen in: the man's card in the fight, the clinic in the settlement screen.

items.title: VIA GROK: THE GROUND PICKS WHO SHOWS UP, THE DAY PICKS HOW MANY
items.why: Grok reports you said there is no scripted first fight: the part of the map you stand on picks which faction's pool a party comes from, and the day count, your crew's strength and your level pick its size, Battle Brothers' shape. You see it as which crews roam which part of the valley on the map and who stands across the board when a fight opens.

show.src:
VIA GROK, pages GROK_52, GROK_53, GROK_54, GROK_58, GROK_59, GROK_60: the pool by ground; size by roster strength (the 12 strongest men, 10 plus 2 a level past 1), days and the job's skulls; a camp already on the map scales by days and distance, not the crew. Matches his fifth vote (no authored first fight).

Seen in: the map's roaming crews, the enemy line-up when a fight opens.

items.title: VIA GROK: THE PLAYER NEVER READS A TILE'S NAME; FACTIONS ARE BANNERS AND PARTIES
items.why: Grok reports you said the player does not see street or ground names on the map, the way Battle Brothers never labels its ground, and a faction shows itself as a banner and a party you can tap. You see it on the map: no labels on the land, a banner over every crew.

show.src:
VIA GROK, pages GROK_56, GROK_57, GROK_58: no tile labels; a party on the map shows a banner and its name when tapped; the ground still picks the pool underneath. Grok's own name lists (GROK_55, GROK_57) are marked bad votes by him and are not locked.

Seen in: the map (no ground labels; banners over crews), the party card on a tap.

items.title: VIA GROK: GAS MOVES TO THE AMMO PILE
items.why: Grok reports you moved gas out of the resources pile into the ammo pile on 10/2, so a car's shot spends gas and a pistol's shot spends bullets or nails from the same ammo count. You see it in the top bar's ammo number and at the stall.

show.src:
VIA GROK, pages GROK_45, GROK_64, GROK_70: the ammo pile holds a gas can and loose bullets and nails as one skin; a pistol shot takes bullets or nails; a car shot takes gas; 10 batteries a bundle. His newer line (10/2) beats the older six piles (10/1) where they clash.

Seen in: the top bar's ammo count, the stall in the settlement screen, the car's shot in the fight.

items.title: VIA GROK: UNTIL THE BATTLE BROTHERS FIGHT IS RIGHT, THE GAME IS BATTLE BROTHERS
items.why: Grok reports you said the Rogue Fable pieces, the beat and the dial, wait until the Battle Brothers recreation is right, because they would make it more fun later, not now. You see it in the demo's fight: turns, no beat, no dial.

show.src:
VIA GROK, pages GROK_71, GROK_72, GROK_75: the fight is Battle Brothers until he is happy; the beat line and the dial are later pieces; the gambit comes later and needs research; a combat tile stays a house. Matches rules 63 and 63a (the dial is next, not dead).

items.title: SETTLEMENTS AT NIGHT, AND NO TWO ALIKE
items.why: The camp is fuller, every size of settlement now comes in two versions, and each has a night picture lit only by the street lamps and fire barrels that still burn. Thumbs up and the settlement screen uses these, and you see it in the settlement screen when you enter a place at night.

items.title: THE FIGHT FITS A PHONE ON ITS SIDE, A TABLET AND A COMPUTER
items.why: Turn the phone sideways or open the fight on a computer and the bar becomes Battle Brothers' one-row bar, face and bars left, skills middle, WAIT and END TURN right, so the board keeps at least two thirds of the screen instead of half. Rotate your phone in a fight and you see it, in the VOTE tab and the demo, NOT IN A TAB YET.

items.title: NIGHT IS A COLOUR, NOT A DARKNESS: THE NIGHT FIGHT MUST READ IN FULL SUN
items.why: You loved the night and its street lights but could not see at its darkest, so the night now gets a measured floor: the ground never drops below a fifth of white, a man always stands out three to one from his ground, and the same frame still passes with a quarter of white glare added like sun on the glass. You see it in the demo's night fight and on the map at night, and later as a brightness slider in SETTINGS.

show.src:

items.title: THE FIGHT'S BAR, FINISHED
items.why: The fight's bar now uses the game's own lettering, reads from the left with a printed mark on each tag, shows the cut edge of the cardboard, and never cuts a hint off mid-word. You see it at the bottom of every fight, and when you tap his face.

items.title: THE AMBIENCE COMES DOWN
items.why: You said it's loud, so the sign, the block lights and the generator hum now play at half volume (A), with B even lower and C as before, and only the loudness changed. You hear it in the VOTE tab under LOOK, and in the game everywhere those hums play.

items.title: THE NIGHT FIGHT YOU CAN PLAY IN THE SUN
items.why: Night is now a cool moonlit colour instead of a black wash, keeping about two thirds of the day's light, the lamp pools stand three to one over the dark, and the men get a thin moon rim so they never sink into the ground. Hold the phone outside in a night fight and you see it, in the VOTE tab and the demo, NOT IN A TAB YET.

items.title: THE TURN CLOSES
items.why: The END TURN button in the new fight is silent, so this gives it a short steel click, like a bolt dropping into its notch. You hear it in the VOTE tab under LOOK, and it goes on END TURN in the fight once you say yes.

items.title: ONE SONG AT A TIME: THE FIGHT TAKES THE MUSIC, HOME GIVES IT BACK
items.why: The map's song used to keep playing under every fight, and coming home from a fight left the map silent; now the fight takes over with its own song and the map's song comes back after the fight's song finishes its phrase. You hear it here, recorded from the demo itself, and on the DEMO's map in any fight.

items.title: NIGHT YOU CAN STILL SEE IN THE SUN
items.why: You love the night but said it was too hard to see outside, so every settlement night is now a cool colour instead of near black, and the lamp pools are bright enough to pick out from the dark, measured against the readability floor. Thumbs up and night stays this bright, and you see it in the settlement screen at night.

items.title: SETTINGS, WITH BRIGHTNESS
items.why: Settings is now taped-up cardboard and receipts with separate music and sound levels and a brightness slider, so you can play outside in the sun. You see it behind the gear in the game, and the start screen will open it too.

items.title: THE SETTLEMENT IS ONE PICTURE, THE BUILDINGS ARE IN IT
items.why: You said the buildings looked like options, so the place is now one painted 45-degree picture with the barber, stall, posts, clinic, board and junk lot standing in it, and a building lights up and says its name only when you touch it. You see it in the VOTE tab under LOOK, and in the demo every time you arrive at a place.

items.title: THE ROAD IS FASTER
items.why: Travel on the map was silent, so this is your party's footsteps on a paved road at the faster road pace. You hear it in the VOTE tab under LOOK, in the travel clip on the map's sounds page.

items.title: DIRT IS SLOWER
items.why: The same footsteps on open dirt, at the slower pace dirt costs you. You hear it in the VOTE tab under LOOK, in the travel clip on the map's sounds page.

items.title: THE NIGHT HAS INSECTS
items.why: Night travel was silent, so this is many insects calling, built from real clicks and never a hiss. You hear it in the VOTE tab under LOOK, in the travel clip on the map's sounds page.

items.title: THE START SCREEN'S LOOK
items.why: The crew picks are now cardboard cards, a posted sheet of origins with your pick ringed in marker, and a paper form for the name, and the start screen has its look: a taped card, a receipt and a cracked glass pane over the valley at night. You see it the moment the game opens, on the picks now and on the start screen once its buttons are wired in.

items.title: THE FIRST FIGHT IS A FEW THUGS BY THE MATH, NOT ONE AND NOT TWELVE
items.why: You said twelve against twelve cannot be the flow and asked for just one enemy so you can test the rest, so the road's parties are now sized by Battle Brothers' own math (your strength, the days, the difficulty, the ground) and on day one near the start that math gives two or three thugs, never a hand-placed single man. You see it in the demo's first fight after the start screen, and later in bigger parties as the days pass.

show.src:
Rule 75b; RUN [a few, not twelve], COMBAT [the enemy math]. The count words are Battle Brothers': a few 2-3, some 4-6, many 7-10, lots 11-13.

Seen in: the demo's first fight; the party's count word on the map when the clock stops.

items.title: THE GAS STATION AND THE MOTEL IN A FIGHT
items.why: The gas pumps under the canopy are cover that can catch fire if hit, and you can stand up on the motel's walkway as high ground. Thumbs up and these rules stay, and you see it in the COMBAT tab when a fight starts on main street.

items.title: THE CHURCH AND THE SCHOOL IN A FIGHT
items.why: The church's front steps are low cover, the school's fence is cover you can see through, and the school's flat roof is high ground. Thumbs up and these rules stay, and you see it in the COMBAT tab when a fight starts on main street.

items.title: THE WAREHOUSE AND THE CASINO BACK IN A FIGHT
items.why: The warehouse's loading dock is high ground and the dumpsters behind the casino are cover. Thumbs up and these rules stay, and you see it in the COMBAT tab when a fight starts in the works.

items.title: THE FIGHT OPENS WITH YOUR LINE, AND YOU SET IT
items.why: Your men now open in Battle Brothers' two rows of nine, fighters in front and shooters behind, and nothing moves until you tap FIGHT, so you can tap a man and drop him on any tile of your two lit columns first. Start any fight by hand and you see it, in the VOTE tab and the demo, NOT IN A TAB YET.

items.title: A START SCREEN: NEW GAME, CONTINUE, SETTINGS
items.why: The demo now opens on a title, dressed by the UI chat in our materials, with NEW GAME (your crew picks), CONTINUE (your saved day, straight in) and SETTINGS, instead of dropping you on the loading screen. You see it the moment you open the DEMO, upright or on its side.

items.title: THE SAME FIGHT BOARD ON A PHONE, A TABLET AND A COMPUTER
items.why: Every fight board now has a ring of the same city around it that you can see but not walk on, so a sideways phone, a tablet and a computer all open on the whole fight with no black bars. Thumbs up and the fight opens like this on every screen, and you see it in the COMBAT tab when a fight starts.

items.title: THE MARKET: A SMITH AND AN ARMOURER IN THE PLACE
items.why: You said there was nowhere to buy weapons or armour, so a camp now has one guns-and-plate stall and a town or fortress a smith and an armourer, stocked from Battle Brothers' own lists in our names at ten crowns a battery, and the board shows each job's skulls and pay. You see it in the VOTE tab under LOOK, and in the demo when you tap the smith or armourer in a place.

items.title: THE TITLE SHOWS IN TWO SECONDS AND THE WORLD LOADS BEHIND IT
items.why: You loved the new opening screen but waited forty seconds for it, so the title now has to paint within two seconds of your tap while the world loads behind it, with NEW GAME lighting up when it is ready and the loading shown as the camera's own feed instead of a bar. You see it the moment you open the demo on your phone.

items.title: THE SETTLEMENT'S LABELS
items.why: A building now names itself on a torn paper tag only while your finger is on it, and the prices and pay inside print on receipt lines you can read in the sun. You see it in any settlement, when you touch a building and when you open the stall or the board.

items.title: DAY 1 IS A FEW THUGS, DAY 100 IS A LEADER AND MARAUDERS
items.why: The fight now takes the party the map hands it and dresses it by the days and the difficulty, Battle Brothers' way: early it is thugs and a lesser raider in cheap gear, late a leader, armoured marauders and marksmen with twice the armour. Compare the two parties in this card and you see it, in the VOTE tab and the demo once the map sends parties, NOT IN A TAB YET.

items.title: YOUR ORIGIN DECIDES WHO YOU START WITH
items.why: Picking THE LONE WOLF now starts you as one level-4 fighter alone, THE BLOCK WATCH as twelve neighbours who can field sixteen, and every origin's men, money and caps come from Battle Brothers' own fifteen. You see it on the door's origin cards after NEW GAME, and in your first fight in the DEMO.

items.title: YOUR BAG: 36 SLOTS, AND WHAT YOU BUY LANDS IN IT
items.why: You said you still could not buy weapons, so every shop is now two grids like Battle Brothers, their shelf of icons on top and your 36-slot bag under it, and buying moves the item into the bag for its price while selling takes it out. You see it in the VOTE tab under LOOK, and in the demo at the smith, the armourer or a camp's guns-and-plate stall.

items.title: HOLD A FINGER ON A WEAPON AND IT SAYS WHAT IT DOES
items.why: Every weapon now has a card: our name, its Battle Brothers base, one plain line, and its real numbers (damage, armour, reach, AP), with the car door's line under it when he carries one. Hold a finger on the strike square or on any man in a fight and you see it, in the VOTE tab and the demo, NOT IN A TAB YET.

items.title: THE TITLE IS DETUNED
items.why: The start screen was silent, so this is a slow theme on a drifting, slipping tape through a dead broadcast, with the loading room's hum underneath. You hear it in the VOTE tab under LOOK, on the title's music page with two comparisons.

items.title: THE BARBER'S CLIPPERS
items.why: The barber was silent, so now a tap plays a mains clipper's blade striking its stop, a real 120 Hz buzz. You hear it in the VOTE tab on the settlement's answers page.

items.title: A CAN ON THE COUNTER
items.why: The stall was silent, so now a tap plays a tin can's own ring landing on the wood counter, two materials in one contact. You hear it in the VOTE tab on the settlement's answers page.

items.title: THE BOARD'S OWN NAIL
items.why: The board was silent, so now a tap plays a tack pinning a card, the same strike the fight's turn-close uses, smaller and higher. You hear it in the VOTE tab on the settlement's answers page.

items.title: PAPER AGAINST THE POST
items.why: The posts were silent, so now a tap plays many tiny paper creases catching and releasing, broadband. You hear it in the VOTE tab on the settlement's answers page.

items.title: EVERY ITEM IS AN ICON
items.why: All 310 weapons and armour pieces now have their own drawn icon, a pipe or a fire axe or a hard hat, each with its own tape, rust and wear so no two look the same. You see it on every line at the smith, the armourer and the stall, and it is what the inventory bag will show.

items.title: EVERY BRIGAND FIGHTS LIKE HIS BATTLE BROTHERS SELF
items.why: Thugs rush the nearest man, a raider with a pike waits for his line and then hits from two tiles, the marksman shoots the shieldless rookie and backs off, and the leader hangs back keeping his men brave, each from its wiki page. Play this clip or any fight against a mixed band and you see it, in the VOTE tab and the demo, NOT IN A TAB YET.

items.title: A PLACE HAS TRAITS: THE SAME TOWN RAIDED, AND ON MARKET DAY
items.why: You said settlements have traits from random rolls, so a place now rolls Battle Brothers-style situations: raided burns a house and raises prices with nobody hiring, sickness boards the clinic, market day fills the street and drops prices, and the keeper tells you first. You see it in the VOTE tab under LOOK, the same town rolled two ways side by side, and in the demo whenever you arrive somewhere.

items.title: THE FIRST ROAD GIVES A FEW THUGS, NOT NINE
items.why: Every fight used to throw the same nine brigands at you; now a party's size comes from Battle Brothers' math (your crew's strength, the days, the difficulty), so day one gives two thugs and day one hundred gives twelve with a leader. You see it in your first fight on the DEMO's map, before on the left and now on the right.

items.title: THE FIGHT BOARDS SNAP TOGETHER LIKE LEGOS
items.why: Every fight block now joins only where its edges match, so streets, curbs and lane lines run straight through and the overpass lands on a real street at both ends. Thumbs up and every board is built this way, and you see it in the COMBAT tab on the freeway fight.

items.title: THE MAP'S BAR AND THE SIX
items.why: The six supplies are drawn as little objects now (a battery, a tin, a first-aid box, cartridges, tape, a water bottle), and the map's bar and speed buttons wear the same cardboard, receipt and glass as the fight and the settlement, readable in the sun. You see it on the map, across the top and in the bottom right.

items.title: VIA GROK: THE FIRST BIG CRISIS COMES AROUND DAY 100
items.why: Grok reports you said the first big crisis lands around day 100 with the fifty days before it getting harder, and the wiki agrees, so act one's first big turn takes that clock. You see it only as text in the VOTE tab for now, and in the game as rumours at the bar from day 50 and the turn around day 100.

items.why: Grok reports Lone Wolf is your favourite start (one man, avoid big groups early), so the door marks it as the hard one and your pick while a stranger's default stays the three-man New Company that Battle Brothers itself opens on. You see it on the start screen's origin sheet: Lone Wolf ringed as the hard pick.

items.title: WHAT IS DATA, WHAT IS NOT
items.why: Research, nothing changed: the new fight already reads its weapons, enemies and rules from files a modder can edit, but the start screen still drops a new origin and the old fight has none of it. You see it in the VOTE tab under LOOK, two lists of what is in a file and what is still in code.

items.title: YOUR COMPANY: TWO LINES OF NINE, AND GEAR FROM THE BAG
items.why: Your twelve stand in Battle Brothers' front and back lines drawn from the fight's own people, you drag them between lines, and a tap opens a man's card with his stats and stars, four gear slots, wage and one pain line, where you drag a gun from your bag onto his hands. You see it in the VOTE tab under LOOK, NOT IN A TAB YET in the demo until the run gives it a door.

items.title: EVERY BATTLE BROTHERS CONTRACT, AS A JOB IN OUR VALLEY
items.why: All 49 Battle Brothers contract kinds are now jobs in Vegas, each with who gives it, what it pays and what can go wrong, so the job board can fill itself from this. You see it only as text in the VOTE tab for now, and in the game on the board in every place.

show.src: Eight kinds of job: haul, carry, clear, hunt, patrol, hold, recover, find. Each one comes from a town's trouble, and finishing it fixes that trouble.

items.title: HOW MUCH OF THE VALLEY WORKS IN EACH ACT.
items.why: Act one stays at the demo's 12 percent lit, acts two and three start higher, and a past where you tore places down lights less than doing nothing. You see it only as text in the VOTE tab, nothing is drawn yet.

show.src:
ACT ONE: 12% lit, medieval stalls (grain, water, rope, iron tools, lamp oil, salt).
ACT TWO: 20% lit if you did nothing, more if you built, less if you tore down. Stalls add cells, wire, solar film, medicine.
ACT THREE: 30% lit by default, techy stalls (cells, chips, solar film, printed parts).
A ruin you caused stays a ruin. Not drawn yet.

items.title: VIA GROK: THE TURNS ARE TOO SHORT, SO EVERY MOVE YOU DID NOT MAKE TAKES A BEAT YOU CAN SEE
items.why: Grok reports you said the turns are too short, which I read as the enemy's moves and AUTO's resolving too fast to follow, so each move you did not make now plays over at least one second with the mover lit and its number shown, your own turn has no timer, and a tap skips to the end. You see it in the demo's fight on the enemy's turn; thumb down if you meant something else and say what.

show.src:
VIA GROK, pages GROK_131-133 ('Paolo said the turns are too short'). COMBAT [a turn you can read]. A turn is still a beat (9/22) for your own men; this is about the time the OTHER side's moves take on the glass.

Seen in: the demo's fight, the enemy's turn and AUTO.

items.title: A DAY ON THE MAP IN TWENTY SECONDS
items.why: A whole day on the real map in twenty seconds: parties walk with a reason, never stand on each other, leave fading footprints in their colour, and market-day towns have a bigger crowd at the gate. You see it in the VOTE tab under LOOK, filmed from the game's own camera.

items.title: THE SHOP PRICES NOW COME FROM THE WIKI, NOT A GUESS
items.why: Every weapon, hire and job pay in the game now traces back to Battle Brothers' own numbers, turned into batteries at ten to one with nothing ever cheaper than one. You see it in the MARKET tab once it is wired in, where the sell price will move with how much a town likes you instead of sitting at one flat number.

items.why: The same valley twice, how fast you cross each ground beside how tightly one crew owns it, and the quickest way across runs straight through the ground held hardest, like the Strip at 92 percent one outfit. You see it in the VOTE tab under LOOK, two maps side by side.

items.not_a_map_picture: this item shows a contact sheet (before, after, and a 1:1 crop) because the row asks for before and after; the map picture itself is slices/vote/COOK_THE_FAR_END_SHEET.png and the bank, which run 1.05 against DIRECTION's floor of 1.5
items.title: THE FAR END, PAINTED BY HAND
items.why: The whole valley from altitude is painted now instead of noise: real ranges with lit and shadowed faces, the basin they ring, the city grid, the strip's spine, the dead airport, the washes and the lake, all read off the game's own map. You see it in the VOTE tab, before and after side by side.

items.title: A BATTLE BROTHERS MONSTER THAT IS NOT AN ANIMAL BECOMES A MACHINE FROM THE ROBOTICS PLANT
items.why: Your beast law says every beast is a lab-made real animal, but nineteen of Battle Brothers' beasts are folklore monsters that never lived, so those become the machines of the robotics plant by the airport (the Unhold a two-legged cargo loader, the Nachzehrer a scavenger bot that eats bodies for parts) while real animals stay lab-made and each keeps its Battle Brothers fight lesson exactly. You see it in the fight when one of them walks onto the board and in its card's one line.

show.src:
Rule 81 (coordinator default). WORDS found the gap (8607f623); COMBAT re-tags six mislabelled rows and adds a kind column (animal, machine, man). His locks stand: a boss is never an animal, no radiation, only what real DNA allows.

Seen in: the fight (a machine on the board), the enemy's card, the recap.

items.title: WHAT EACH DIFFICULTY CHANGES
items.why: Battle Brothers has two difficulty settings, fights and money, plus Ironman, and these three wiki tables show what each one changes while our game has one number for all of it. You see it in the VOTE tab under LOOK, as three tables.

items.title: A SMALL FIGHT GETS A SMALL BOARD, AND IT OPENS ZOOMED IN
items.why: The fight board is now cut to the parties, your line and theirs five houses apart with a house of room round them, so three thugs against your twelve is about 9 by 10 instead of 20 by 15, and it opens on your line with the man at full size. Start any fight and you see it, in the VOTE tab and the demo, NOT IN A TAB YET.

items.title: THE DATA FILES ON ONE PAGE
items.why: For modders: all 15 data files on one page, built from the real files, with what each holds, who reads it, and how to make the knife hit harder by changing one row. You see it in the VOTE tab under LOOK; tap a file.

items.title: THE FREEWAY IS THE STREET'S ROAD, WITH NO WALL ON IT
items.why: The freeway now uses the street's own asphalt, paint and curb, with a low concrete barrier down the middle and a see-through fence at the edges instead of the grey wall. Thumbs up and every freeway fight looks like this, and you see it in the COMBAT tab on the freeway board.

items.title: TEN PEOPLE WHO STOP YOU ON THE ROAD
items.why: Ten real Battle Brothers road events, each now a person in Vegas who stops you with two choices and the price on the button, and moving on is always free. You see it only as text in the VOTE tab, and in the game on the map's roads.

show.src: A trader with a dead trike, a posse with a photo of one of your men, a blind man with a watch, kids who stoned a battery trader, a thief taped to a dead street light, and five more.

items.title: THE FIGHT'S CLIPS
items.why: In the fight men now breathe while they wait, and a man struck down sinks and crawls while the dead lie flat, so you tell down from dead at a glance. You see it in the VOTE tab under LOOK, before beside now on the beat.
items.said: I wanna see all my character art that we worked so hard on live in the game, even if it's new combat

items.title: THE DEMO, EVERY SCREEN, MARKED
items.why: Every screen a stranger meets, shot on a phone, with what is right in gold and what is slop in red, and the biggest hole is not a pixel: tap a place and nothing opens, and the fight ends with nothing saying you won. You see it in the VOTE tab under LOOK, one marked picture per screen.

items.title: EVERY NUMBER THE FIGHT FEELS
items.why: The demo's fight now reads every number from one list and each has a source, 71 from the Battle Brothers wiki and the rest your own rulings and words, and the fight script types none of its own. You see it in the VOTE tab under LOOK, all 85, green for the wiki and red for yours.

items.title: THE MODS FOLDER
items.why: A design, nothing built: a mod is a small folder named like the data file it changes, and eleven checks show an empty folder or a broken mod changes nothing while a good mod changes exactly what it says. You see it in the VOTE tab under LOOK.

items.title: THE RUMOUR AT THE BAR
items.why: Buy the bar keeper a drink and he tells you where good gear is, a pin drops on the map and slowly fades, and sometimes he is wrong while strangers lie more. You see it only as text in the VOTE tab, and in the game at the bar in every place.

show.src: Twelve rumours: a locked arsenal off the Strip, a flooded casino vault, the tunnels under Hoover Dam, the robotics plant, a cold lab vault, and seven more.

items.title: THE BAR: A ROUND FOR THE CREW, AND A RUMOUR
items.why: Like Battle Brothers' tavern, a round costs a battery a head, up to four a night, lifts the crew's spirits and the town's opinion of you, and each round the keeper tells you a different rumour that can mark a place on your map. You see it in the VOTE tab under LOOK, and in the demo when you tap the bar in any place.

items.title: ABOUT 42% OF YOUR CREW CARRIES ON. YOU PICK OLDER OR YOUNGER.
items.why: When you enter act two or three about 42 percent of the last crew carries on, strongest first, and you pick whether your own relative arrives older or younger, which is saved but does not change a face yet. You see it in the VOTE tab as text, and in the game on the phone's offer row.

show.src: Four people in the old crew: the two strongest carry on, the two weakest are left behind. One person always carries. The OLD and YNG buttons sit beside M, F and OK on the phone when you enter a new act.

items.title: A DAY ON THE ROAD COSTS DIFFERENT FOOD IN DIFFERENT PLACES
items.why: A six-man company eats 18 points of food a day crossing the desert and heals two injuries' worth of medicine, against 12 food points on flat ground, straight from Battle Brothers' own numbers. You see it in the records, not drawn yet, feeding the road's upkeep once the day clock reads it.

items.title: THE WORKS FIGHT AT THREE SIZES
items.why: A small fight now gets a small board of this place, a bigger fight a middle one, and only the endgame gets the big board, all with the streets joining. Thumbs up and fights are cut to the party like this, and you see it in the COMBAT tab when a fight starts.

items.title: THE PLACES WORTH GOING TO
items.why: The six places with the god gear, each ring sized by how many guard it, and the hollow red ring is a library this valley never rolled, so a bar rumour can send you after a building that is not there. You see it in the VOTE tab under LOOK, on the valley map.

items.title: THE FAR END AS TILES
items.why: The map draws your whole valley at one pixel per cell, 9,216 pixels against Battle Brothers' two million, which is why it looks like a tan dome: there is no mountain painting in it at all, only a flat colour and a speckle. These are sixteen painted pixels a cell instead, so you see it in the VOTE tab with the old map beside it.
items.not_a_map_picture: this item shows a contact sheet; the map pictures are slices/vote/COOK_THE_FAR_END_TILED.png and the tile bank

items.title: WHAT A SETTLEMENT PAYS YOU
items.why: Battle Brothers pays about one seventh of what you paid when you sell gear back, and slide a price to compare its big town, its small village and our shop side by side. You see it in the VOTE tab under LOOK.

items.title: THE WEAPON FILE
items.why: For modders, nothing changed in the game: a weapon can list two skills but the fight plays only the first, so 27 skills never show, and three optional fields would fix it without changing any weapon. You see it in the VOTE tab under LOOK.

items.title: WHAT YOUR MAN PASSES TO HIS HEIR: HALF HIS LEVEL, HALF HIS PERKS, ALL HIS GEAR.
items.why: A man's heir starts at half his level with the first half of his perks, his gear, his house and his stars, never his body or wounds, so a level earned in act one means something later. You see it only as text in the VOTE tab, since nothing shows levels yet.

show.src:
Level 7 man: heir level 4, grandchild level 2.
Perks: the first half he took.
Gear and house: kept.
Debt: never crosses (corrected).
Body, wounds, age: never.

items.title: HOW THE DEMO ENDS
items.why: Three jobs from one woman at the Wash, haul water, run off the road crew and clear the dog lot, and the lot becomes yours, then a thanks screen opens NOTES. You see it only as text in the VOTE tab, and in the demo on the Wash's board.

show.src: The last thing she hands you is the big dog's ear tag. It has a lab number and your company's name on it, and nobody explains why.

items.title: THE SMITH'S HAMMER
items.why: The smith's forge was silent, so now a tap plays an anvil's own low, short ring, the mass of the stump bleeding it away fast. You hear it in the VOTE tab on the soundscape's first two page.

items.title: THE ARMOURER'S RIVETS
items.why: The armourer's bench was silent, so now a tap plays four quick, tiny strikes setting a rivet, a gun's own working cadence. You hear it in the VOTE tab on the soundscape's first two page.

items.title: THEIR TURN TAKES A SECOND A MOVE, AND A TAP SKIPS IT
items.why: Every move of theirs (and of your men on AUTO) now holds the board for two beats, one second at 120, the mover lit, the camera on him, and the man hit shows his chance and what it cost him; your own turn has no timer, and a tap on the board skips the rest of theirs. Play a fight and let them move and you see it, in the VOTE tab and the demo, NOT IN A TAB YET.

items.title: THE CLINIC: PAY TO HALVE A WOUND
items.why: Like Battle Brothers' temple, the clinic lists every hurt man with his injury and days left, and paying halves the days at the wiki's own price, 20 crowns a day left and more for a higher level, with a hired medic taking a day more. You see it in the VOTE tab under LOOK, and in the demo when you tap the clinic in any place.

items.title: FIGHT VERDICT 22: THE FREEWAY AGAINST THE STREET
items.why: The wall across the freeway is gone and it shares the street's road now, and what still looks like another game is marked: a flat barrier, loud orange lines, a box trailer, gold rings, and the fight shows the sharp art blurry. You see it in the VOTE tab under LOOK, the marked fight picture.

items.title: GOOD BROS AT THE POST
items.why: Six real recruits rolled fresh each time from the wiki's own stats and prices, with real names from the same system every person in the game uses. You see it in the VOTE tab under LOOK, and in the game at the hall in every place.

items.title: BUILD IN A TOWN YOU HOLD
items.why: Building is a spot you tap on the town picture: in a town someone else holds your own voice says it is not your ground, and in your base the list of eight things costs a battery each and stands there the next day. You see it in the VOTE tab under LOOK, three pictures side by side.

items.title: A JOB PAYS MORE IF YOU PUSH, AND PUSHING COSTS YOU
items.why: The same job pays 76 batteries taken straight or up to 80 if you push for more pay, straight off Battle Brothers' own haggle math, but every push costs relations whether it works or not. You see it in the records, not drawn yet, feeding the board's contract cards once RUN TWO wires it in.

items.title: FOUR FACTIONS WITH A FACE
items.why: Four factions, road crews, the house, the dead and the beasts, each get a banner colour, a party size, one want and one line. You see it in the VOTE tab under LOOK, NOT IN A TAB YET on the live map.

items.why: On a phone-speed processor NEW GAME is ready only after about 85 seconds with 30 MB downloaded first, and a patch handed to RUN cuts that download to 9 MB, but the wait stays because the processor is the wall (most of it is baking character art the map does not show yet). You see it on the demo's start screen, where the loading bar runs that long before NEW GAME lights.

items.title: A FIGHT INSIDE A DEAD CASINO
items.why: A new fight board inside a dead Strip casino: slot machines and card tables are cover, the cashier's cage is the high ground, and at night only a few machines and fires give light. Thumbs up and the Strip's fights happen in here, and you see it in the COMBAT tab on the casino board.

items.title: THE PHONE IN THE BAR'S HAND
items.why: The cracked phone on the map keeps its crack but now uses the game's own letters and brighter ink, so every post reads in the sun, and the family faces are cardboard cards, the one you are lit amber like the speed button. You see it on the map, the phone in the top right.

items.title: THE ROADS
items.why: Every road in the valley lit and timed: the freeway brightest at full speed, the boulevards just under it, then the dirt and the washes, and I checked thirty different valleys to prove every settlement can reach every other on paved road alone. Measuring it caught a six-lane Las Vegas boulevard rated slower than driving across open desert, because the road was being averaged in with the shops and flats beside it, and you see it in the VOTE tab under LOOK, NOT IN A TAB YET on a play surface.

items.title: THE PARTIES WALK
items.why: On the map you now travel as three people, you and two of your company walking at your shoulders, and every roaming party walks and slides between blocks instead of standing still and jumping. When the clock stops everybody stops and breathes, and you see it before beside now in the VOTE tab and on the MAP while you travel.
items.said: every party on the map is drawn and moving

items.title: TWO THINGS FROM GROK, TESTED AGAINST YOUR OWN RULES. TWO HOLES.
items.why: Two of Grok's ideas checked against your rulings: the ground-picks-who-shows-up idea still counts factions as territory, which you ruled out, and a crisis at day 100 would outlast an act of about 130 days. You see it only as text in the VOTE tab, in the card below.

show.src: 1. THE GROUND PICKS WHO SHOWS UP: holds, but it reads who holds land. You ruled home bases and roaming parties, not territory. Fix: base the pool on the 14 home bases.\n2. THE CRISIS CLOCK: matches our own 'foretold, not optional' law. But a crisis from day 100 for up to 100 days outlasts a 130-day act. My default: the crisis is the act's ending.

items.title: WHEN THE AMMO RUNS OUT
items.why: In Battle Brothers ammo is cheap but limited, one company stock refilling a 10-shot quiver after each fight, and our game has no stock yet so scarcity cannot be felt. You see it in the VOTE tab under LOOK: pick a start and a gun and count the fights before you reach for a blade.

items.title: A MODDER'S FIRST HOUR
items.why: For modders, seven steps from nothing to a changed game, each one working today but one, and the knife step was run for real: two numbers changed in one file and the knife hits 20 to 30. You see it in the VOTE tab under LOOK.

items.title: A SOUND IS A RECORDING OF THE REAL OBJECT, OR BUILT FROM ITS REAL PHYSICS, NEVER NOISE
items.why: You killed the sand-noise recipe and said sounds come from real material, and the sounds chat builds each sound from its object's physics rather than recording it, so this asks whether physics counts or only a recording of the thing. You hear it in the settlement, where the smith's hammer and the armourer's rivets are built from physics today.

show.src:
The second votes (NO SAND, sounds from real material); SOUNDS' better-than line (f4b96771: 'every sound synthesized from its object's real physics, never a sample file'). Thumb up: physics counts. Thumb down: record the real thing.

Heard in: the settlement screen's taps, the fight's shots and hits.

items.title: THE DEMO TOWN'S JOB BOARD, FULL
items.why: Eight small side jobs around the Wash, from a missing kid to running a clinic box, each on the same road as one of the three ending jobs, so the board is never empty in the first 30 minutes. You see it only as text in the VOTE tab, and in the demo on the Wash's board.

show.src: Dona Ortiz wants her kid found, Ruben the smith wants his wire back, Sarge wants the road walked, and five more at the Wash and the two camps nearby.

items.title: BATTLE BROTHERS ALREADY PRICES MERCY, THREE WAYS
items.why: Saving everyone pays the same as always unless you fail, taking everything pays more at a real cliff, and the mercy option gives up the job's pay for something else entirely, all straight off Battle Brothers' own contracts. You see it in the records, not drawn yet, feeding DYNASTY's ending work.

records/BOHEMIA_ECONOMY_DAY_60_THE_PRICE_OF_MERCY_BATTLE_BROTHERS_ALREADY_CHARGES_IT_10_9_26.md; banks/BOHEMIA_ECONOMY_TEST_LINES_9_5_26.md round 60.

Seen in: not drawn yet, feeds DYNASTY [the ending].

items.title: THE POSTS: SEE THE HIRE BEFORE YOU PAY
items.why: At the hall every recruit is a card with their face, background, eight stats with the starred one in gold, and their price, a camp two, a town four, a fortress six and more on market day, and paying puts them on your roster with their gear in your bag. You see it in the VOTE tab under LOOK, and in the demo when you tap the hall in any place.

items.title: ARMOUR YOU CAN SEE
items.why: One man in five armours, nothing bought then padded, leather, mail and plate, each a real piece sorted from the real Battle Brothers gear list by how tough it actually is. Thumbs up, and you see it here first, then on the roster and in the fight once the other chats wire a bought piece to this table.

items.title: THE MAP AT EVERY STOP, AGAINST BATTLE BROTHERS
items.why: The map is sharp now and the far end is painted, but one pinch skips the whole middle, the city sits on a raised slab, and every lot is the same grit. You see it on the map, close up and pinched all the way out.

items.title: THE SETTLEMENT PICTURES, FINISHED
items.why: The camp, the town and the fortress are painted over now: rain stains down the walls, the ground worn along the paths between the buildings you can actually use, a painted sign over each one, trash where people stand, and at night the open doors spilling light on the dirt. You see it in the VOTE tab, the town before and after, day and night.

items.title: WHAT YOU BUILT, ON THE MAP
items.why: What you build in a town now stands beside that town on the map the next morning, pays into your own purse, and counts in the future your kids inherit. You see it on the map at your base: the left shot is before, the right is the next morning with a wall and a tank.

items.title: WHAT EACH GROUND DOES TO A FIGHT
items.why: Thirteen fight boards, one for every kind of ground in the valley, each cut from the real city so you can see what a fight on it is actually like: the near empty one is the open desert, the near solid one is the mountain, and the eleven between them are the town. Measuring it caught our own numbers saying every ground in the valley was about half blocked when the real boards run from one and a half per cent to ninety six, and you see it in the VOTE tab under LOOK, NOT IN A TAB YET on a play surface.

items.title: THE TOWN IS ALIVE
items.why: The town screen gets its people: keepers at their doors smoke and wait, the stall keeper haggles, a hire leans at the posts, people walk past, and when your finger comes near a building its keeper looks up and waves you in. You see it ten seconds at a time in the VOTE tab, and in the town screen itself once RUN TWO places them (NOT IN A TAB YET).
items.said: the settlement screen is one painted place

items.title: THE SAME STREETS IN THE FUTURE, GROWN OR FALLEN
items.why: Every fight board now has a reclaimed future (solar roofs, gardens, every lamp lit) and a raided one (burnt roofs, scorch, rubble, lamps dead) on the same streets. Thumbs up and fights in later acts look like this, and you see it in the COMBAT tab once the acts are wired in.

items.title: THE RESHUFFLE IS AN ARROW
items.why: The little question mark on each family face that gives them a new name is now a drawn try-again arrow on its own glass button under the face, big enough for a thumb, so a tap on the face still switches who you are. You see it on the map, on the phone, under the faces of your family.

items.title: NEW GAME READY 20 SECONDS SOONER ON A PHONE, SAME PICTURES
items.why: The game was fitting the same people's bodies to their skeletons 1,256 times while it loaded, and only 174 were different, so a fix that does each one once (and draws every pixel exactly the same) cuts the phone-speed wait for NEW GAME from 87 to 67 seconds. You see it on the demo's start screen once RUN applies it: the loading bar finishes sooner.

items.title: WHAT THE FLIP IS IN THE STORY: A, B OR C. I PICK A, AND I FIXED A FLAW.
items.why: Three ideas for what the flip is in the story, and my pick is A, the old machine's model of your family, never named until the ending. You see it in the VOTE tab, in this card's text.

show.src:
A. The machine's model of your family. Free to build. The flip can only show what was recorded, so it is wrong about everything you did off the feed. That is the ending's gauge, already.
B. Upload and genes. A grandchild shares 25 percent of your DNA, a whole mind cannot be copied by 2045, and it makes your family the fake one.
C. The box twist. If the past is a recording, nothing you do changes the future, which breaks the three-acts rule.
Pick A, B or C.

items.title: WHAT A RESPEC COSTS
items.why: Battle Brothers resets a man's perks with a Potion of Oblivion for seven rare monster parts and 5,000 crowns, and your swap-one-mastery idea is a smaller version at 25 to 50 batteries and a few days. You see it in the VOTE tab, the two side by side.

items.title: HOW BIG IS TOO BIG
items.why: A modded knife that hits for minus 5 used to load silently, and now it loads with a warning that never blocks, so a mod can still beat anything in the game. You see it in the VOTE tab when you type any number into this card.

items.title: OLD VERSUS YOUNG IS A TRADE: SLOW HEALING, BUT A HEAD START.
items.why: Nobody ever reaches forty or sixty in play, so the OLD and YNG buttons are the only ageing there is: old heals slower and tires sooner, young learns faster with fewer perks. You see it in the VOTE tab, on this card.

show.src: YNG (twenties): heals fast, learns fast, fewer perks to start.\nOLD (forties to fifties): injuries last about 1.5 times longer, tires sooner, small print needs glasses. But he starts with more of the family's perks and his aim does not drift.\nNobody dies of old age inside an act, so these are the only ages you will see.

items.title: THE BAR ON ONE TOWN
items.why: Every town keeps a 0 to 100 bar that moves with what you do, using Battle Brothers' own bands and numbers. You see it in the VOTE tab: one town after a job, a stolen loaf and an attack.

items.title: HOW HARD IS A KILLER
items.why: Every recruit hides stars on three stats and a 7-star killer is 1 in 18, so 36 killers is really 12 per act and no harder than Battle Brothers. You see it in the VOTE tab when you slide the bar on this card.

items.title: ON A FLIPPED PHONE THE MAN STAYS FULL SIZE
items.why: Setting your line with the phone on its side used to shrink your men to 15 pixels to fit the column; now they stay at their full 112 and a drag pans the rest, the same on the computer and the tablet. Turn your phone sideways before FIGHT and you see it, in the VOTE tab and the demo, NOT IN A TAB YET.

items.title: WHAT YOU BUILT, IN THE FIGHT
items.why: A fight at a place you built on now stands on what you built: your wall is cover in front of your line, the water tank blocks, and a roof is high ground for your man. You see it in a fight at your base, the same fight before and after.

items.title: THE FLIP IN FOUR BEATS
items.why: Today flipping to act 3 changes nothing in the world, so here is the real one: the phone's tape tears, the world goes dark, a hard cut to the same spot in the other year, and the first time an act opens the changes rise on the beat. You see it on the map, drawn over the game's own frames in four beats.

items.title: THE ORIGIN CREWS
items.why: Three starting companies at their real size, the Lone Wolf's one veteran in worn plate, three companions in mail, and the Block Watch's twelve weak men in work clothes, every man's gear sorted from the real Battle Brothers data by how equipped his background actually is. Thumbs up, and you see it here first, then at the door once RUN wires a pick to this table.

items.title: THE WEED THAT DRINKS THE RIVER AND SALTS THE GROUND
items.why: Battle Brothers never lets you plant anything, so this is real desert science: tamarisk drains and salts the ground, cheatgrass turns a once-a-generation fire into a yearly one, and a date palm takes years to feed your grandkids while a hog feeds you once. You see it in the records, not drawn yet, feeding TUNING and LIFE and CITY.

records/BOHEMIA_ECONOMY_DAY_61_WHAT_GROWS_THE_WEED_THAT_DRINKS_THE_RIVER_AND_SALTS_THE_GROUND_10_9_26.md; banks/BOHEMIA_ECONOMY_TEST_LINES_9_5_26.md round 61.

Seen in: not drawn yet, feeds TUNING and LIFE+CITY.

items.title: THE SHOT KICKS
items.why: In the fight a shot used to be a man standing still with his gun up; now the gun kicks into his shoulder, he rocks back and settles, and a pistol flips higher than a rifle. Three men fire one after another and you see it before beside now in the VOTE tab (in the fight itself once COMBAT reads the clip table, NOT IN A TAB YET).
items.said: re-create Battle Brothers combat

items.title: THE FREEWAY KIT
items.why: The freeway kit: a barrier run, a see-through shoulder fence, a freeway lamp, a sign gantry, a stalled truck and a burned car, every one at its real size with its height named so the board knows what stops a shot. You see it in the VOTE tab, all six laid on the asphalt they belong on.

items.title: THE SIX BUILDINGS' PROPS
items.why: The six new buildings had nothing in them, so here is one prop each: pumps for the gas station, pews spilling out of the church, a school fence with a gate in it, the motel ice machine, warehouse pallets and slot machines dumped in the casino's back lot, every one at its real size with its height named so the board knows what stops a shot. You see it in the VOTE tab, all six with their sizes on them.

items.title: HIS BLOCK, AS A PLACE YOU ARRIVE AT
items.why: The three settlement screens are sizes, not places: camp, town and fortress are how big a town is, and none of them is anywhere. This is the fourth one and it is your own block, with your door and your step, your drive with the wreck still on it, next door's gate shut and his table out, and the board at the kerb, and you see it in the VOTE tab by day and at night.

items.title: CLIMBING: A MAN'S CARD BEFORE AND AFTER A FIGHT
items.why: After a won fight each man gets his XP, at 200 he hits level 2, three stats go up in green by his stars, and he picks one of nine first-tier perks that he carries into the next fight. You see it in the VOTE tab under LOOK, before on the left and after on the right.

items.title: THE CELLS THAT ALL OPEN THE SAME FIGHT
items.why: The whole valley coloured by which fight board each cell loads, and the lit ones all load the SAME board: the airfield, the speedway, the stadium, every civic building, and three of the six big gear places. Twenty four of our seventy eight kinds of place fall through to one fallback, which is more than any real board gets, and you see it in the VOTE tab under LOOK, NOT IN A TAB YET on a play surface.

items.title: THE FREEWAY'S FIVE WRONG PIECES, FIXED
items.why: The barrier is now cast concrete, the lines are the street's white and a faded yellow instead of orange, the trailer is a real rusted box, the asphalt is patched and cracked, and the dark band is gone. Thumbs up and the freeway looks like this in every fight, and you see it in the COMBAT tab on the freeway board.

items.title: THE TITLE SHOWS UP IN 2.7 SECONDS ON A PHONE, WAS 3.5
items.why: The old fight that the demo never opens was still half of the page a phone downloads, so the demo is now cut without it and the title comes up in 2.7 seconds instead of 3.5 on a phone-speed processor (the goal is 2). You see it on the demo's start screen: the title and its buttons show up sooner after you tap the link.

items.title: HAIRSTYLES THAT MATCH
items.why: The hair picker showed the right 11 names but lost two of its six dials every time you clicked one, so three cuts drew the same cap and one lost its texture; both are wired now, worst pair down from 93% identical to 89%. You see it in the VOTE tab.

items.title: THE WHOLE CROWD MATCHES
items.why: Every citizen in the valley got a random hair texture on their portrait instead of their real one; 76 of 82 textured citizens disagreed with their own body. Fixed and shipped, not a vote -- you see it in the VOTE tab as proof.

items.title: THE ENEMY FACES
items.why: Every brigand tier's portrait had none of its own dressed body's haircut, not even by accident; now all six wear the real cut, and the leader's face gets a second light so he reads as the one you remember. You see it in the VOTE tab.

items.title: THE KEEPERS SPEAK
items.why: The smith now has a real price line to say, with a real trait line and a real rumour already waiting on the same mouth. You see it in the VOTE tab, item THE KEEPERS SPEAK.

items.title: BY GENERATION THREE THE VALLEY SHOULD REMEMBER ONE STORY, A LITTLE WRONG.
items.why: Right now a deed fades but is never forgotten, while real people remember the name, one merged story and the grudges still alive. You see it in the VOTE tab, on this card.

show.src: Measured: seven retold deeds went through two generations and all seven were still there, just fainter.\nReal memory: the name lasts, the details drift, one story absorbs the rest.\nProposal: generation three keeps the name, ONE legend line (a little wrong), living grudges, and a place name. The rest is gone.

items.title: THE PHONE SHOWS THE JOBS
items.why: The phone now shows the two nearest places that are hiring and what they pay, with skulls for the danger; it shows them but never takes them, you take a job at the place, and a job you took disappears from the phone. You see it on the map, at the top of the phone.

items.title: AN ID IS A PROMISE
items.why: A mod finds every row by its id, so renaming one of the 725 ids breaks the 764 places that point at them. You see it in the VOTE tab, with the four rules that keep mods working.

items.title: EVERY ROLL A MAN MAKES
items.why: The wiki's stars, level and XP numbers on one page, with a red box where the demo differs: 1 to 3 starred stats instead of exactly 3, random level-up stats, and wages that never rise. You see it in the VOTE tab, on its own page.

items.title: VIA GROK: A MISSED PAYDAY MAKES A HIRE LEAVE A COUPLE OF DAYS AFTER THE BATTERIES HIT ZERO, NEVER THE SAME DAY
items.why: Grok reports you said a hire who is not paid walks only a couple of days after your batteries hit zero, not the same day, and his traits stretch or shrink that clock (a greedy man sooner). You see it on the roster screen as a man's mood dropping after the missed noon and his leaving on the second or third morning.

show.src:
VIA GROK, pages GROK_141 and GROK_143 (the wiki's Mood page: not paid is -1 mood, greedy -2, not eaten -1; angry 0 to 15 percent may desert; mood drifts back when nothing happens). The wiki gives no day count; his 'a couple of days' is the number.

Seen in: the roster screen's mood line; the morning a man is gone.

items.title: A TOWN BEFORE AND AFTER A RAID
items.why: A crew that reaches a town unopposed leaves it raided (half the items, half the recruits), and a caravan leaves it well supplied, using Battle Brothers' own two pages. You see it in the VOTE tab: two towns on one real valley, before and after.

items.title: EVERY SETTLEMENT HAS ITS OWN SHELF, NEVER ITS OWN PRICE
items.why: Battle Brothers moves a town's price with raids and supply; ours keeps the one-battery price locked and moves the SHELF instead, cut thin after a raid and fuller on market day. You see it in the records, not drawn yet, feeding TUNING and the settlement screen.
