items.title: THE PEOPLE OF THE PLACE: KEEPERS AT THEIR DOORS, A CROWD BY THE STALL
items.why: COOK's finished pictures are in, and now a keeper breathes, smokes or haggles at every door while a crowd by the stall swells to eleven on market day and drops to one when the town is raided or sick. You see it in the VOTE tab under LOOK, and in the demo when you arrive at any town.

items.title: THE FOUR PHONES: CRACKED, REPAIRED, THE SLAB, YELLOWED
items.why: Your phone at each act, rendered live on the game's own phone: cracked in act 1, taped in a rubber bumper in act 2, a clean metal slab if act 3 went well, yellowed and shattered if it went badly. You see it on the map's phone, four versions side by side.

items.title: DO THE THIRTEEN STILL READ APART, SMALL
items.why: Battle Brothers reads a man's kit by shape, not colour, because its camera is often far, so I shrank all thirteen gang looks down to a small figure and measured whether each one is still its own shape or colour. Thumbs up, and you see it here, with two pairs honestly flagged as the closest calls for DIRECTION and COOK to look at.

items.title: THE THREE BLOCKS THE VALLEY NEEDS
items.why: Four fight boards: the stadium bowl, the water plant, the hospital, and a casino floor with two hundred slot machines on it. The first three are cut from the real city, the hospital is a solid slab because nothing in this whole valley has an inside you can walk into, and the casino is the one room anybody ever built and no part of the game can currently reach it, and you see it in the VOTE tab under LOOK, NOT IN A TAB YET on a play surface.

items.title: A NEW PHONE OPENS ON THE START SCREEN, NOT IN THE CITY
items.why: A test walk skipped the start screen by clicking the hidden BEGIN behind it, so the game looked like it dropped strangers mid-game; now nothing but NEW GAME or CONTINUE gets you in, and the screen stays dark until the start screen is drawn. items.title: WHO DIES AT ZERO, AND WHAT THE OTHERS CARRY HOME

items.title: FOUR LEGS
items.why: The first lab-made beast moves: a dire wolf walks in, breaks into a lope with a moment in the air, bites the man with its jaws open, takes his swing and goes down, three pictures a beat like the men. items.title: THE LONG INJURY

items.title: THE BAR'S GLASS
items.why: A glass set down on the bar counter had no sound, and now it rings once, clear and short, like real glass. You hear it in the VOTE tab on its own page.

items.title: A DEATH SHOULD COST THE LIVING WORK. AND I FIXED A BUG OF MINE.
items.why: Nobody buries anybody in the game yet, and debts no longer pass to heirs, matching your ruling that debts die. You see it in the VOTE tab, where the heir's first day carries the body, the creditor, the house and the name.

items.title: MODS TO COPY
items.why: Seven whole example mods, from adding an enemy to changing a wage or a helmet, each with its patch, its one lesson and what the checker said. You see it in the VOTE tab when you tap one; the game does not load a mods folder yet.

items.title: WHEN A MAN WALKS
items.why: In Battle Brothers each unpaid day drops a man one mood step and only an angry man deserts, so a content hire walks on day 3, your 'couple of days'. You see it in the VOTE tab when you slide the days unpaid and change his nature.

items.title: AN ACT IS ONE FELT YEAR: 130 DAYS, FOUR SEASONS, ABOUT 30 NAMED MOMENTS.
items.why: The plan said a season per act, but the game has no seasons, so each act gets four seasons and about 30 named moments, with four reports telling the 35 years between acts. You see it in the VOTE tab, on this card.

show.src: FOUND: the game has no season or calendar, and keeps only 30 nights of history.\nPROPOSED: 130 days an act in four seasons of about 32 days. About one memorable event in every four days, each named in the feed.\nThe 35 years between acts are told by four reports: what the valley looks like, who is left, what the valley says of you, what you left standing.

items.title: THE STASH: SIX SUPPLIES AND HOW MANY DAYS EACH LASTS
items.why: Each of the six shows its count and what it buys you, so 50 food for four men on desert is 4 days, 2 hurt men burn 2 meds a day, and 30 rounds are 15 shots, with the wage due at noon and what the next town sells. You see it in the VOTE tab under LOOK; in the demo it opens when you tap the six in the top bar, once RUN wires it.

items.title: WHEN A SETTLEMENT COMES FOR YOU
items.why: Wrong a faction twice and its patrols hunt you and its caravans open to raiding, then it cools off by itself, using the two thresholds Battle Brothers states. You see it in the VOTE tab: one faction through two bad contracts and then the quiet mornings after.

items.title: WHEN THE DATA CHANGES
items.why: In eight days the data folder changed 44 times and only once could it break a mod, and four lines of policy, a version number, a written-for tag, a break note and a made changelog, keep it that way. You see it in the VOTE tab, on this card.

items.title: THE ROAD ITSELF CHARGES, THE TWIST HAS ONE REAL PRICE
items.why: Battle Brothers never prices distance, it just rolls more trouble on a longer road; one job states its own twist price in writing (lose some mules, lose half the pay). You see it in the records, not drawn yet, feeding TUNING and the settlement screen.

items.title: A RAID ON YOUR BASE
items.why: Once you build at your base, a crew comes for it: your phone tells you it is coming, if you are home you fight it at your gate on what you built, and if you stay away for four days they take the base. You see it on the map and the phone, then in the fight at your gate.

items.title: A BLOCK IS TWO THINGS TOUCHING
items.why: A parry was a dull filtered thud, and now it is a blade's edge catching a shield's wood-and-metal rim with a real bright click. You hear it in the VOTE tab on its own page.

items.title: THE MARKET AGAINST THE WIKI
items.why: The shop sells back at one seventh like Battle Brothers, but still ignores town size, your standing and 32 situations like a siege or a fair. You see it in the VOTE tab, at the bottom of the prices page.

items.title: A POLICE STATION FULL OF HOSPITAL WARDS
items.why: The same police station drawn twice: same walls, same doors, same rooms, because both are the game's own floor plan maker given the same building. The one on the right is what the game actually builds today, and fifteen of its nineteen rooms are hospital wards, because the table that picks the rooms exists in two places and the copies disagree, and you see it in the VOTE tab under LOOK, NOT IN A TAB YET on a play surface.

items.title: THE FIGHT'S GROUND, SHARP
items.why: Close in, the fight's ground is now drawn straight from the original art, one art pixel on one screen pixel of the phone, where before it was shrunk to a third and blown back up; a tile keeps all its edges (106 percent of the file, it kept 32), and it still runs at 60 frames by day and by night. Open any fight and you see it in the asphalt, the cars and the lamps, in the VOTE tab and the demo, NOT IN A TAB YET.

items.title: THE THREE BODIES
items.why: Your face already runs in the family through the three generations, so I built the same thing for the body, one ancestor's shape pulling at his son and grandson by the same pull your face uses. You see it here, three men in the same clothes with three different builds, not three strangers.

items.title: WHEN THE PHONE TURNS
items.why: When you turn your phone sideways, the in-game phone used to run off the bottom of the screen under the speed buttons; now it moves to the left side and fits, the speed buttons keep the bottom right, and nothing covers anything. You see it on the map when you hold your phone sideways.

items.title: HOW FAR EACH WEAPON REACHES
items.why: Every weapon's reach on one chart in the VOTE tab, against your rule that melee hits at 1 and every gun starts at 2. Melee all pass. But a bow can only hit at exactly 7 tiles and our rifle only at exactly 6, because the data copied each weapon's farthest reach into its nearest reach. The pistol is a dagger, so it hits at 1.

items.title: PATCH INSIDE A LIST
items.why: For whoever makes mods. A weapon has lists inside it, like skills. A mod can now change one entry by name or position, or add and remove words, without copying the whole list. Two new example mods show it. Also: the range tool you voted down is gone.

items.title: WHO GUARDS THE SIX PLACES
items.why: Each of the six legendary places is guarded by whoever holds its ground, sized by how hard the place is. You see it in the VOTE tab: six cards with the guard and what it is made of.

items.title: THE ROSTER SHOWS THE HURT: A MAN'S CARD BEFORE AND AFTER HE IS STRUCK DOWN
items.why: A man struck down in a fight leaves the line for LAID UP, and his card counts down his 30 to 40 days, names the injury he keeps for good, says it in one pain line and prices the clinic, and dragging him back into the line is refused. You see it in the VOTE tab under LOOK, before on the left and after on the right.

items.title: THE TWIN: OUR GROUND AGAINST THE PACK YOU BOUGHT
items.why: You were right: our road, props and fight board beside your approved pack tiles at the same size, and the pack has 100 times the colour, real cracks, dark outlines and painted objects where ours has flat stamps. You see it in the fight's ground, ours on the left, your pack on the right.
